around.headline: Bengaluru man loses Rs 81,000 to fake bank 'verification' call
around.summary: A Bengaluru man lost Rs 81,000 after a caller posing as a bank representative talked him through a bogus 'verification' process over the phone and extracted his card and OTP details, per The Times of India. If a caller claims to be from your bank and asks for an OTP or CVV to 'block' a transaction, hang up and call the number printed on the back of your card instead.

around.headline: Bengaluru mob attacks family after mistaking love marriage for a kidnapping, 6 hurt
around.summary: A crowd attacked a family and chased their car after wrongly believing a young woman who had married her partner was being kidnapped, injuring six people before police stepped in and made four arrests, per India Today and Deccan Herald. If you witness a public scene that looks like a kidnapping, call police (100) rather than joining a crowd acting on assumptions.

around.headline: Traffic restrictions across Bengaluru for Ganesha immersion processions on September 18
around.summary: Bengaluru traffic police have announced diversions and restrictions for Ganesha idol immersion processions on September 18, per The New Indian Express and Deccan Herald. If your commute passes near lake routes or procession paths that day, plan for delays or an alternate route.
around.source: The New Indian Express, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Maurya Circle-Race Course Road shut for two months for white-topping work
around.summary: The Maurya Circle to Race Course Road stretch has been closed for about two months for white-topping work, per Deccan Herald, adding to the city's ongoing post-rain traffic strain. Commuters on this stretch should plan an alternate route for the duration of the closure.

around.headline: Bengaluru police begin shifting 11,346 seized vehicles off footpaths
around.summary: Bengaluru police have started moving 11,346 vehicles that were seized and left clogging footpaths outside police stations, some for years, to yards on the city's outskirts, per The Indian Express and The Hindu. If you have an old seized-vehicle case pending, it's worth checking with your local station while the clearance is underway.

around.headline: UPI transaction charge plan draws backlash from businesses, challenged in Supreme Court
around.summary: A Centre proposal to levy charges on UPI transactions above Rs 2,000 has drawn criticism from Bengaluru businesses and is now being challenged in the Supreme Court, per The Times of India and Live Law. If you routinely make larger UPI payments for business or rent, watch for updates before any charges take effect.
around.source: The Times of India, Live Law

around.headline: US House passes bill seeking up to 100% tariffs on India over Russia trade
around.summary: The US House of Representatives passed a Russia sanctions bill that could impose tariffs of up to 100% on India and other countries continuing to trade with Russia, per The Hindu. This adds pressure on India-US trade talks and could eventually affect prices of imported goods and export-driven jobs.

street_smart.title: You get a call from someone claiming to be your bank's fraud department, saying suspicious activity was flagged on your credit card and they need to 'verify' you immediately to block it — like the Bengaluru man who lost Rs 81,000 this way today. The caller already knows your name and the last four digits of your card, and calmly talks you through 'verification' as the call continues. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Times of India, Sept 16-17 — a Bengaluru man lost Rs 81,000 after a caller posing as a bank representative for 'verification' convinced him to share sensitive card and OTP details over a phone call framed as fraud prevention. This fake-bank-verification-call mechanism (OTP/social-engineering fraud) hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: The call sounds urgent and professional, and it mentions your bank's name and your card's last four digits — details that make it feel legitimate.

choices.text: Hang up immediately without sharing anything, then call your bank's official number printed on the back of your card (never a number the caller gives you) to check if anything is actually wrong.
choices.feedback: Correct. Banks never call asking you to reveal an OTP, CVV or full card number for 'verification' — genuine fraud alerts are handled by blocking the card, not by soliciting your secret codes. Calling the official number yourself removes the scammer's ability to control the conversation.

choices.text: Since the caller already knew your name and card's last four digits, assume they must be from the bank, and read out the OTP that arrives by SMS so they can 'block the suspicious transaction.'
choices.feedback: This is the trap. Scammers often already have your name, phone number and partial card number from earlier data leaks, which is exactly what makes the call sound legitimate — that stolen credibility is then used to extract the one thing they don't have: your OTP. Reading it out completes a fraudulent transaction; it doesn't block one.

choices.text: Don't give the OTP, but confirm your full 16-digit card number and CVV when asked, since the caller says that's needed to look up your account.
choices.feedback: Risky. Sharing the full card number and CVV is nearly as dangerous as sharing the OTP — combined with an OTP intercepted later, that's enough to complete a transaction. A genuine bank representative can already see your account from your registered number and never needs your CVV read aloud.

choices.text: Stay on the line and ask the caller detailed questions to test whether they're genuine, since hanging up abruptly feels rude and you want to be sure before blocking your own card.
choices.feedback: Risky. Practiced scammers are prepared for pushback and can talk convincingly for several minutes, using that time to build trust or manufacture panic. The safer move is to disengage immediately and verify independently rather than try to out-question a trained con artist.

takeaways: Banks and card networks never ask for your OTP, CVV or full card number over a phone call — not even for 'verification' or to 'block' a fraud transaction.
If a caller creates urgency, hang up and call the number on the back of your card or use the bank's official app — never a number the caller provides.
Turn on SMS/app transaction alerts and consider a lower default transaction limit on your card, so a single OTP slip can't drain your account.

quiz.question: How much money did a Bengaluru man lose this week to a caller posing as a bank representative for 'verification', per The Times of India?
quiz.why: Genuine banks never ask for an OTP or CVV over a phone call — any 'verification' call asking for these should be treated as fraud.

quiz.question: Bengaluru traffic police have announced restrictions for Ganesha idol immersion processions on which date?
quiz.why: Expect diversions near lake routes and procession paths on that day if your commute passes through those areas.

quiz.question: A bill passed by the US House of Representatives this week over Russia sanctions could impose tariffs of up to what rate on countries like India that trade with Russia?
quiz.why: The bill still needs Senate approval and presidential action to become law, but it adds pressure to ongoing India-US trade talks.

quiz.question: Under India's Constitution, what is the minimum age to become a member of the Lok Sabha?
quiz.why: The minimum age is higher for the Rajya Sabha (30 years) and for the President and Vice-President (35 years).

quiz.question: Which Indian state has the longest coastline?
quiz.why: Gujarat's coastline runs to roughly 1,600 km, ahead of Andhra Pradesh's, which is the second-longest.
